title: KIN-SYS Protocol: Institutional Deployment and Cross-Installation Federation Reference Implementation
description: KIN-SYS is a provider-neutral, software-first protocol architecture for governing and verifying digital instructions across institutional and jurisdictional boundaries. This 0.2.0 research/reference release records the engineering milestone merged to the main branch at commit b9385003509541cc5e014ca4a5a271323eaf3872. It extends the runnable synthetic governed-execution prototype with institutional deployment and versioned domain records; institution-owned MINAH deployment and binding lifecycle contracts; tenant-scoped identity-provider registration and OIDC adapter selection; signed actor assertions and versioned delegated-authority grants; issuer/receiver trust administration; Ed25519-signed, destination-bound cross-installation messages and acknowledgements; bounded HTTPS/mTLS transport components; PostgreSQL-backed federation inbox/outbox and replay controls; and PostgreSQL tenant-isolation policies. The repository includes reference implementations, migration scripts, architecture and security-boundary documentation, integration tests, and reproducible demonstration/report workflows. CI on the exact main merge commit completed successfully: 789 tests run, 4 skipped, 0 failures; the four skipped tests require a separately configured live OIDC test profile. This evidence is limited to the checked-in test fixtures and CI environment. This is not a production deployment or independent security certification. Institutional registries, identity providers, authority evidence, MINAH deployments, jurisdictional sources and trust/key material still include synthetic, injected or local reference components. The complete two-installation runtime is not yet proven across independent hosts and independent database services; the PostgreSQL federation fixtures use two databases on one CI PostgreSQL service and execute the installation adapters in one process. The live mTLS process-boundary test uses a minimal receiver stub rather than the full institutional runtime. Live OIDC provider tests were skipped. All 29 routes in the production API implementation matrix remain NOT_IMPLEMENTED_AS_PRODUCTION_HTTP_ROUTE; the OpenAPI document and matrix are planning contracts, not routed production endpoints; no real funds move; exactly-once execution across network and CEE/IVM stores is not claimed. PostgreSQL row-level security uses transaction-scoped tenant context and must be deployed with a least-privilege non-superuser role without BYPASSRLS; custom session context alone is not a boundary against arbitrary SQL executed under the same database principal. Production use requires institution-specific integration, deployment hardening, independent security review, operational controls and acceptance testing.
